news.title: Should OpenAI Be Afraid of Jensen Huang?
news.summary: News flash: A lot of people in Silicon Valley are afraid of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang . They have understandable reasons to be fearful, as Leo, Phoebe and I detailed in our story this morning. The chipmaker has a lot of money and influence to throw around, since Huang has the ear of several top government officials, including President Trump . More importantly for model developers like OpenAI , Nvidia controls the flow of AI chips they need to develop and run today’s most advanced models. It’s been hard enough for AI developers to get access to those chips, so it makes sense that the companies would want to avoid anything that might upset Huang. This has led to a situation where OpenAI has avoided taking a public stance on the current debate over chip sales to China for fear of alienating Nvidia and Huang, which generates plenty of revenue from Chinese companies and wants access to the Chinese market itself. (Nvidia isn’t allowed to sell its most advanced tech directly to that market, but Chinese firms like ByteDance and DeepSeek still find a way to access the chips outside China’s borders or through smuggled hardware .)

items.title: Should OpenAI Be Afraid of Jensen Huang?
items.summary: News flash: A lot of people in Silicon Valley are afraid of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang . They have understandable reasons to be fearful, as Leo, Phoebe and I detailed in our story this morning. The chipmaker has a lot of money and influence to throw around, since Huang has the ear of several top government officials, including President Trump . More importantly for model developers like OpenAI , Nvidia controls the flow of AI chips they need to develop and run today’s most advanced models. It’s been hard enough for AI developers to get access to those chips, so it makes sense that the companies would want to avoid anything that might upset Huang. This has led to a situation where OpenAI has avoided taking a public stance on the current debate over chip sales to China for fear of alienating Nvidia and Huang, which generates plenty of revenue from Chinese companies and wants access to the Chinese market itself. (Nvidia isn’t allowed to sell its most advanced tech directly to that market, but Chinese firms like ByteDance and DeepSeek still find a way to access the chips outside China’s borders or through smuggled hardware .)

items.title: How Nvidia Uses Its Soft Power to Influence Customers and Shape Policy

They also directed staffers to speak to members of the global affairs team working on new export control policies, rather than discussing it on Slack. Chip restrictions are a delicate topic at the company. news.title: Palantir and Shopify Both Beat Earnings. Their Stocks are Falling Anyway.
news.summary: Apple, Palantir, Shopify, and several other major companies just reported earnings, and Wall Street is sending a clear message: Beating expectations isn't enough when profit margins are under pressure. In this video, Eric Bleeker, CFA, Chief Investment Officer of 24/7 Wall St., breaks down the biggest earnings movers and what their results reveal about the stock market. Apple (Nasdaq: AAPL) beat revenue and earnings expectations as iPhone sales surged 17.5%, but disappointing gross margins raised concerns. Palantir (Nasdaq: PLTR) delivered explosive 96% revenue growth, yet investors are questioning slower growth in U.S. commercial contract value. Shopify (NYSE: SHOP) plunged 16% after missing revenue expectations and disappointing on free cash flow, despite beating earnings estimates. Elsewhere, Revvity (NYSE: RVTY) rallied 9% after raising guidance, while Fiserv (Nasdaq: FISV) jumped 10% on stronger earnings and expanded cost-cutting plans. Meanwhile, Zebra Technologies (Nasdaq: ZBRA) tumbled 16% despite beating estimates and raising its outlook, and Dynatrace (NYSE: DT) cut earnings guidance due to margin pressures. The big takeaway? Investors are increasingly focused on profitability, margins, and forward guidance rather than headline earnings beats alone.

news.title: Elon Musk Got Turned Down by 3 Phone Giants. Now SpaceX Is Eyeing Boost Mobile as a Shortcut Around a $300 Billion Build.
news.summary: Eric Bleeker of 24/7 Wall St. looks at why SpaceX (NASDAQ: SPCX) may be eyeing Boost Mobile after Verizon (NYSE: VZ), AT&T (NYSE: T) and T-Mobile (NASDAQ: TMUS) reportedly turned Elon Musk down as a phone partner. The Washington Post reported on November 2nd that SpaceX has been in talks to buy Boost from EchoStar (NASDAQ: SATS) or partner with it. Nothing has been signed, and the structure is still open. The appeal is speed and cost. TD Cowen analyst Gregory Williams estimates a national network from scratch would cost upwards of $80 billion and take years. Verizon's CEO put the build at four to six years and $300 billion to $500 billion. Musk says two to three years. Boost brings customers, a brand and spectrum, and SpaceX already agreed to buy some EchoStar spectrum licenses for about $17 billion. T-Mobile's CEO sees no room for a SpaceX MVNO, though he is open to a resale deal for a complementary satellite product. AT&T closed its EchoStar spectrum deal in the third quarter. Verizon added 406,000 postpaid phone net additions, AT&T added 379,000, and T-Mobile raised full-year guidance. The catch is that Boost leases network access from AT&T and T-Mobile, and a change of control could let both end those agreements. Watch whether that risk derails any deal.

news.title_zh: AMD 上漲 5%，Intel 上漲 4%，Marvell 上漲 2%，晶片股在 AMD 財報前反彈
news.summary_zh: 晶片股在 AMD 季報前強力反彈，但 Intel 的嚴厲指引已證明，若展望令人失望，強勁的盈餘超預期也無濟於事。瞭解 AMD 需交付什麼才能維持反彈勢頭。

news.title: Could Marvell Actually Climb 102%? Or Is UBS Totally Wrong?
news.summary: Key TakeawaysMarvell stock is down 45% from its June high, and it fell again after agreeing to buy Lumentum in a $115 billion all-stock deal. UBS kept its Buy rating and $350 price target the next day, which points to 102% upside.
news.title_zh: Marvell 真的能攀升 102% 嗎？還是 UBS 完全錯了？
news.summary_zh: 重點摘要 Marvell 股價較六月高點下跌 45%，並在同意以 $115 billion 全股票交易收購 Lumentum 後再度下跌。UBS 維持買進評級及 $350 目標價，隔日指出有 102% 上漲空間。

news.title: Marvell and Lumentum Fell Hard. Their Supplier’s Stock Is Soaring
news.summary: When Marvell announced a blockbuster acquisition and both stocks tanked, one overlooked supplier quietly posted the best quarter in its history after hours. The question now is whether that record run can survive the deal's fallout.
news.title_zh: Marvell 與 Lumentum 股價重挫。其供應商股價卻飆漲
news.summary_zh: 當 Marvell 宣佈一項大型收購且雙方股價暴跌時，一家被忽視的供應商在盤後靜悄悄地交出了歷來最佳季度表現。現在的問題在於，這波紀錄性表現能否倖存於交易的衝擊之下。
